children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with a basic question:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm responsible for - my son Alex. He's 15 and lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I understand you have a son named Alex who is 15 years old and lives at home with you.

Let me ask you a few more questions to determine your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to understand a bit more about your situation:

**Is Alex in any form of approved education or training, or has he left education? For example, is he attending school, college, or any training program?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's still in school - just doing his GCSEs at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for that information. Just a few more questions:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex? For example, another parent or guardian?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. A couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex in hospital, in care, or in any residential accommodation paid for by your local council?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in hospital or care - he lives at home with me full time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Just one final question:

**Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or is he receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work - he's focused on his schoolwork. And he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name either.

conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:

- Alex is 15 years old (under 16)
- He lives at home with you in the UK
- He's in approved education (attending school and doing his GCSEs)
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- He's not in hospital, care, or residential accommodation
- He hasn't started working 24 hours or more per week
- He's not receiving benefits in his own right

You meet all the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit!

**Important note:** Please be aware that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. However, you can still claim Child Benefit even if this applies to you.

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit through the official government process. Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
